newsitem.title: USA: Mayor-elect seeks housing takeover in New Jersey.
newsitem.headline: Mayor-elect seeks housing takeover in New Jersey.

text.p: Camden's mayor-elect has asked the federal housing agency to take over the city's troubled housing authority, the Camden Courier-Post reported Saturday.

Mayor-elect Milton Milan, in a letter to Housing and Urban Development Secretary Andrew Cuomo, recommended he find the local agency "in substantial default" of its funding contract and replace the managers.
A meeting was scheduled for Monday with regional HUD officials, a spokesman told the newspaper.
The Department of Housing and Urban Development had twice threatened to assume full control of the authority's $13-million budget to run 2,300 dwellings, which house 7,000 tenants.
The Camden agency has been heavily criticised for its inability to maintain its housing stock, despite a federal grant of $42 million.
